lede: The overnight test: can a vision model read our books as well as the Transkribus model (52805), and can its reading help fix the tags and the lines? Everything is scored against the RA's corrected pages (FINAL) in set A, 209 pages from 13 books. No Transkribus credits were spent. Claude ran on the Max plan through claude -p; Gemini 3.8 Flash ran on the Google key.

In short. Claude Opus reads almost as well as Transkribus: 1.6% of characters wrong, against 0.84%. Part of that gap is not real, because FINAL began as Transkribus output. Gemini Flash is much worse at 6.8%. The reading adds nothing to the tags that the picture alone does not give, with one exception: running heads, page numbers and catch-words. For those, comparing the text across consecutive pages halves the errors. It barely helps the lines.
read_intro: Each model got strips of ten printed lines, cut on the RA's own lines, and had to return the text line by line. Scores are the share of characters wrong after evening out quote marks, nikkud and spacing. "Letters only" also ignores punctuation. Each row is compared with Transkribus on exactly the same pages.
read_after: The FINAL bias. The RA started from the Transkribus text and corrected it. Wherever a Transkribus mistake was left in, FINAL agrees with Transkribus and counts against Claude. You can see this by book: on שבע רצון Transkribus scores 0.0% and on one volume of תורת הרמ"ל 0.1%. That only happens if the RA hardly changed anything. On the books where Transkribus has visible errors, Claude is level or better: עשר אורות 1.7% against 2.0%, בית ישראל 1.3% against 1.6%, ספורי אנשי שם 1.1% against 1.0%. Claude's weakest book is תורת הרמ"ל השלם, at 3.1% against 0.7%.

Gemini. Gemini 3.8 Flash makes four times as many errors as Claude, and 80 of its 204 pages are over 5%. Gemini 2.5 Pro loses the line numbering and was dropped after 26 pages. There is no Gemini 3 Pro for text, only an image model.
adjud_intro: I took 20 random lines where Claude and FINAL disagree and looked at the print myself. My count: FINAL is wrong on 6 (lines 4, 6, 7, 12, 14 and 20), both are wrong on 3, Claude is wrong on 8, and 3 I could not settle. The type is small and semi-cursive, so please check my verdicts. Mark who is right; your answers are saved here and I will read them back. If FINAL is wrong on a third of these lines, Claude's true error rate is close to Transkribus's, and both are around 1%.

verdicts.1: Can't tell: ח or ת in חולנית. The sense favours the RA (ח).
verdicts.2: Can't tell: נ"מ or כ"מ; the first letter is damaged.
verdicts.3: Claude dropped the צ: אצילי is right.
verdicts.4: Claude is right: there is a full stop after בשלום. A Yiddish line, which the RA also tagged as a heading.
verdicts.6: Claude is right: מזבח and שלחנו. FINAL kept Transkribus's errors (מבה, יעכשיו, שלחני).
verdicts.7: Claude is right: the full stop at the end of the line is printed.
verdicts.9: Both wrong: FINAL has ויה and חכופה (should be מה and חנופה), and Claude has לכלמדנו.
verdicts.11: Claude normalised the word: the print has שרצונה.
verdicts.12: Claude is right: מצוה, אזי and the commas. FINAL has מביה.
verdicts.13: Claude added a י: the print has וע"כ.
verdicts.14: Claude is right: there is a comma after טהור.
verdicts.16: Both wrong: FINAL has השחות (Claude's השחית is right), but Claude has כנ"ל where the print has כלל.
verdicts.18: Both wrong: FINAL has וע"כ, Claude has ועי"ב, and neither matches the print exactly.
verdicts.19: Claude is wrong: בהקללות and אלהיך, as printed.
verdicts.20: Claude is right: ועריה. FINAL has ועדיה.

layout: Three ways the reading could help the layout. (a) In one call the model reads the lines on our layout and also returns the tags and a list of bad lines (cut, missing, merged). (b) Rules use the text across consecutive pages: a top line that recurs on other pages is a running head; a short top line that reads as a Hebrew numeral is a page number; a single word at the bottom that matches the next page's first word is a catch-word. (c) Lines the model calls "part of a line" are joined to their neighbour on the same baseline.

layout_after: * The 26 example pages are not typical: half were chosen as our worst. The text rules ran on top of our own tags, not on Claude's corrected tags, which so far exist for only 26 pages. Both will be applied together in the real run.
The flags find most bad lines but cannot fix them. A missing or merged line needs a new cut, not a new tag. They are useful as a pointer to the pages you should look at.
next:
• Reading. Claude Opus is a real alternative to Transkribus HTR for these books. It costs nothing on Max, against about half a credit per page, but it is slower, about a minute per page. Before deciding, please settle the 20 lines above. If your verdicts match mine, I would run Claude and Transkribus side by side on one new book, compare where they differ, and look only at those lines.
  • Tags. Production order: YOLO, Claude relabelling with a book note, then the text rules for running heads, page numbers and catch-words.
  • Lines. The reading does not repair lines. The remaining 6% of wrong lines need either a Kraken model trained on our RA lines or the Transkribus line model. Training Kraken is the next experiment.
  • Still respected: no HTR on the new books, no Transkribus credits spent, nothing deleted.
